body: Models with this special rule are ‘Daemonic.’ All Daemonic models have the following universal special rules:
Daemonic Instability • Daemonic Psychology • Fear • Magical Attacks • Unbreakable • Warp-spawned
A character with this special rule cannot join a unit without this special rule, and vice versa.

Daemons are manifestations of pure emotion and raw magic, their physical forms sustained by a tenuous tether to the Realm of Chaos. Their behavior in the mortal realm is driven by the instability of their magical anchors, rather than feeble mortal logic or emotion.
All Daemonic models automatically pass any Fear or Terror tests that they are required to make.

When a unit would normally be required to make a Panic test, a Break test, or elects to Flee as a charge reaction, it must instead test for Daemonic Instability before it Gives Ground, Falls Back in Good Order, or Flees.
If a Daemonic unit Flees for any reason it will always Fall Back in Good Order instead.
How Daemonic units react to disruptions to the Aethyr in the course of battle is further defined by their Daemonic Alignment (see below):
The Blood God's relentless legions care only for the harvest of skulls, rendering Khorne's daemons utterly immune to retreat or distraction.
All Daemons of Khorne automatically pass any Panic tests that they are required to make and cannot choose to Flee as a charge reaction.

Eager to smother their foes in a diseased, loving embrace, the children of Nurgle are relentless in their march towards the foe. Yet, their tether to the mortal realm can be shaken by the rejection of Grandfather Nurgle’s love through the sudden mass banishment of their kin.
All Daemons of Nurgle must test for Panic when required to do so, however they cannot choose to Flee as a charge reaction.

The lithe children of Slaanesh will gladly dance away from an uninspiring charge in pursuit of more stimulating prey, while the sudden, violent, banishment of their kin only anchors them deeper in ecstatic sensation.
All Daemons of Slaanesh automatically pass any Panic tests that they are required to make, however they may choose to Flee as a charge reaction.

Guided by the omniscient foresight of the Architect of Fate, the daemons of Tzeentch will readily dissolve into shifting mist to evade an oncoming charge or they may willingly sever their own tethers to safely vanish from the Material Realm precisely as planned.

Daemons of Tzeentch must test for Panic when required to do so, however, a Daemon of Tzeentch may always choose to fail a Panic test without rolling for Daemonic Instability (even if they would otherwise automatically pass it). Daemons of Tzeentch may choose to Flee as a charge reaction.
When a Daemonic unit is required to make a Daemonic Instability test, the unit must take a Leadership test.
If the natural result of the dice is a 2 or 12 something unexpected immediately happens:

2 – Reality Blinks: Any wounds suffered by the unit during this phase (including any wounds suffered by characters that have joined it) are immediately recovered, and any models removed as casualties during this phase are returned to play, and placed in their previous positions within the unit.

12 – Banished!: Banished!: If the unit contains more than half (50%) of the models it contained at the start of the battle (or more than half its starting Wounds if it is a Character, Monster, or Chariot), it immediately loses half of its remaining models or Wounds, rounding fractions up. However, if the unit has already been reduced to half (50%) or fewer of its starting models or Wounds when this test is taken, it is immediately removed from play and counts as having been destroyed.
If the unit has just lost a round of combat, apply a +1 modifier to the result for every combat result point by which the combat was lost.
If the Daemonic Instability test is passed, the unit suffers no ill effects.

If the test is failed, the unit suffers a number of wounds equal to the amount by which the test was failed. If the unit contains any characters, these wounds are allocated to the unit first until each model has been allocated one wound. Any remaining wounds are then divided as equally as possible between the character(s) and the unit. No armour, ward, or regeneration saves are allowed against wounds suffered in this manner.

If the unit is in combat it must now Give Ground. However, if the unit was in combat and completely destroyed enemy units that were engaged in the combat may attempt to restrain and reform or ‘overrun.’
Friendly Daemonic units within the Battle Standard Bearer's Command range may re-roll any Demonic Instability tests, however they may never re-roll a Banished! result.
Impact Hits caused by this model have an Armour Piercing characteristic shown in the brackets after the name of this special rule.
Violently bound to a solitary cosmic truth, these entities remain completely insulated from the aetheric shockwaves of the battlefield.
This character automatically passes any Panic test that they are required to make.

rows: Reign of ChaosDuring each of their Start of Turn sub-phases, the Daemons of Chaos player rolls a D6 to determine the current ebb and flow of the Winds of Magic, testing whether the local Aethyr is potent enough to sustain the host’s tenuous grip on reality. Note that at the start of the game the Reign of Chaos is always in the ‘Eye of the Storm’ result until the Daemons of Chaos player takes their first turn. On a roll of 1, Chaotic Ebb: The Aethyr dissipates, starving the daemonic host of vital anchoring energy. Until your next Start of Turn sub-phase, all friendly models with the Daemonic special rule have a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered that were caused by a non-magical enemy attack and will generate a “Banished” result on a natural roll of 11 or 12 when making a Leadership Test for Daemonic Instability. On a roll of 2-5, Eye of the Storm: The aetheric currents swirl in a volatile equilibrium; the Daemonic host's tether to reality holds steady.Until your next Start of Turn sub-phase, all friendly models with the Daemonic special rule have a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered and may make Regeneration saves against wounds caused by Magical attacks despite having the Warp-spawned special rule.On a roll of 6, Chaotic Surge: A violent torrent of raw magical power surges across the battlefield, fiercely invigorating the host.Until your next Start of Turn sub-phase, all friendly models with the Daemonic special rule have a 5+ Ward save against any wounds suffered, a 4+ Ward save against any wounds suffered that were caused by a non-magical enemy attack, and may make Regeneration saves against wounds caused by Magical attacks despite having the Warp-spawned special rule. In addition, friendly Daemonic models gain the Immune to Psychology special rule, and generate a “Reality Blinks” result on a natural roll of 2 or 3 when making a Leadership Test for Daemonic Instability.

body: To represent the particularly chaotic relationship between certain gods, certain combinations of Daemonic Alignment are also subject to the following rules:
Khorne and Slaanesh are Rival Alignments. • Nurgle and Tzeentch are Rival Alignments.
Models with a Daemonic Alignment have Hatred (Daemons of (Rival Alignment), Mark of (Rival Alignment)).
Rival Alignments are never considered friendly models for the purposes of casting spells, the Inspiring Presence special rule, or any Daemonic Locus special rules.
Daemons of Khorne have the Furious Charge special rule and during a turn in which it made a charge move, a Daemon of Khorne gains a +1 modifier to its Strength characteristic.

Any enemy model that shoots at a Daemon Of Slaanesh suffers an additional -1 To Hit modifier. Daemons of Slaanesh increase their maximum possible charge range by 1" and have a +1 modifier to the result of any Charge, Pursuit, or Flee roll they make.
The Herald, its mount, and any unit that they have joined gain the Hatred (all enemies) Special Rule.
Notes: A Plagueflail’s Strength modifier and Armour Bane (1) special rule apply only against enemy models the wielder charged this turn.
The Herald and any unit they have joined gain the Regeneration (5+) special rule.
The Herald and any unit they have joined gain the Strike First Special rule.

A Lord of Change does not randomly generate their spells. Instead, they may choose which spells they know from their chosen lore (and may discard one to select that lore's signature spell or a Daemons of Tzeentch spell from the Lore of Daemons.)
The Herald and any unit they have joined may re-roll any Ward Save roll of a natural 1.

A unit of Pink Horrors knows one of the following spells: Glittering Robe from the Lore of Illusion, Pink Fire, or Gift of Mutation from the Lore of Daemons. The unit may cast this spell as a Bound spell:

If the unit includes a Iridescent Horror, it may cast this Bound spell with a Power Level of 1. • If it includes both an Iridescent Horror and a standard bearer, it may cast this Bound spell with a Power Level of 2. • Otherwise, the unit may cast this Bound spell with a Power Level of 0.

A unit with this special rule may perform a ‘Slashing Attack’ against a single enemy unit that is not engaged in combat. To do so, this unit must move (by flying) over the unit it wishes to attack during the Remaining Moves sub-phase. Once this unit’s movement is complete, the enemy unit suffers D3 Strength 4 hits, each with an AP of -1, for each model in this unit that moved over it.

Models within a unit carrying the Standard Of

spell-eater.body: This model may be nominated to attempt a Wizardly Dispel, as if it were a Wizard. For the purposes of Wizardly Dispel attempts, this model counts as a Level 3 Wizard.

armour-of-khorne.body: The Armour of Khorne gives its wearer an armour value of 3+, which cannot be improved in any way.

icon-of-endless-war.body:
When a unit carrying the Icon Of Endless War declares a charge, it may re-roll its Charge roll.

Gifts Of Nurgle

The following Daemonic Gifts can only be purchased by Daemons of Nurgle:

trappings-of-nurgle.body:
The Trappings of Nurgle is a suit of armour that gives its wearer an armour value of 4+ which cannot be improved in any way. In addition, a Wizard with this Gift of Nurgle may wear armour without penalty

Icons Of Nurgle

The following Daemonic Icons can only be purchased by Daemons of Nurgle:

rotten-icon.body:
Enemy units cannot claim any bonus combat result points for being engaged within the flank or rear arc. of a unit carrying the Rotten Icon.

The following Daemonic Gifts can only be purchased by Daemons of Slaanesh:

infernal-enrapturess.body:
Daemonic Heraldsonly. Whilst within this character’s Command range, friendly Daemons

of Slaanesh that are also Wizardsmay apply a +1 modifier to any Casting roll they make. Whilst within this character’s Command range, enemy Wizards suffer a -1 modifier to any Casting roll they make.

siren-song.body: Single use. At the start of your opponent’s Declare Charges & Charge Reactions sub-phase, nominate a single enemy unit that is able to declare a charge against this model (or its unit) within 6”. That enemy unit must declare a charge against this model (or its unit).

enrapturing-gaze.body:
Enemy units engaged in combat with this model cannot use the Inspiring Presence special rule of their General.

Icons Of Slaanesh

The following Daemonic Icons can only be purchased by Daemons of Slaanesh:

banner-of-acquiescence.body: A single enemy unit engaged in combat with the bearer of the Banner of Acquiescence suffers a -D3 modifier to its Weapon Skill and Initiative characteristics (to a minimum of 1).

icon-of-the-eternal-dance.body: Enemy units may not make Stomp Attacks against a unit carrying the Icon of the Eternal Dance.

siren-standard.body:
If an enemy unit charged by a unit carrying the Siren Standard wishes to Flee (or Fire & Flee) as a charge reaction, it must first make a Leadership test. If this test is passed, the unit may Flee (or Fire & Flee). However, if this test is failed, the unit must Hold.

Gifts Of Tzeentch

The following Daemonic Gifts can only be purchased by Daemons of Tzeentch:

will-of-tzeentch.body: Once per round, this model may re-roll a single D6. This may be a D6 rolled on its own, as part of a batch of dice, or as part of a multiple dice roll.

iridescent-corona.body: Any enemy model that targets this model or a unit it has joined, during the Shooting phase suffers an additional -1 To Hit modifier.

twin-heads.body:
Lord of Change only. This model knows spells from two Lores of Magic, rather than the usual one. When choosing the spells that the Lord of Change knows you may discard one spell as normal, replacing it with the signature spell of either Lore of Magic, or with a single Daemons of Tzeentch spell from the Lore of Daemons.

Icons Of Tzeentch

The following Daemonic Icons can only be purchased by Daemons of Tzeentch:

banner-of-discord.body: A unit carrying the Banner of Discord gains the Magic Resistance (-3) special rule. In addition, friendly units within 6" of the model carrying this standard gain the Magic Resistance (-1) special rule.

icon-of-sorcery.body: Pink Horrors only. When a unit carrying the Icon of Sorcery casts Pink Fire from the Lore of Daemons, the Strength of these hits is increased by +1, and their Armour Piercing characteristic is improved by -1, for each point of the casting unit's current Rank Bonus.
